Finite verb; the clause is an asyndetic relative on the written participle `שֹׁמֵעַ`, so the verb keeps only its own English and the supplied 'Who' is its own unit. Folding 'Who' in under rule 46's headless-relative clause was the competing reading, rejected because that clause governs only a relative clause with no antecedent of its own and NUM.24.4 writes `אֲשֶׁר` for this same clause.
The passive participle is recast as 'having ... open'; head on the word carrying the lexeme, discontinuous under rule 25.

Rule 55: a relative supplied for a finite clause juxtaposed to a written antecedent, with no relative morpheme in the Hebrew. Rule 46's headless-relative clause does not reach it, because the participle `שֹׁמֵעַ` stands written before it as the antecedent — the very antecedent NUM.24.4 attaches this clause to with `אֲשֶׁר`. Same treatment as the supplied 'which' of NUM.24.6.
Rule 18's closing sentence: a supplied possessive with no possessive morpheme present.

review_notes: The supplied 'Who' of 'Who seeth the vision of the Almighty' is added under rule 55: the Hebrew writes no relative here, and the participle `שֹׁמֵעַ` standing before the clause is its antecedent, which puts it outside rule 46's headless-relative clause. NUM.24.4 writes `אֲשֶׁר` for the same clause and gives it the word under rule 46's first rider; that written morpheme is the whole of the difference between the two verses.
This brings the verse into line with NUM.24.6, where the supplied 'which' before 'Jehovah hath planted' is already added.
'He ... who heareth' is rule 46's supplied noun phrase for the bare participle and is untouched.
